## What is already strong (keep investing here)

1. **Automated architecture contracts** — Design-token drift (arbitrary hex / px caps), `moduleRegistry` stability labels, no stubbed non-experimental actions, `stateVersion` expectations, banned root overlay hacks, and **required `data-testid` hooks** on a small set of critical surfaces (`TopStatusBar`, `ThreadRail`, `WorkspacePanel`, `WorkbenchRail`, `SettingsDrawer`, `CommandPalette`) are encoded in tests. 2. **Production build hygiene** — Vite splits **react / motion / icons / zustand / misc** vendors, strips `console.*` in minified output, and you recently aligned **lazy vs static imports** so Rollup’s module graph matches reality (fewer misleading splits).

3. **Breadth of E2E** — Dozens of Playwright specs under `e2e/` give you regression safety for commercial/operator flows—many products never get this far.

4. **Security-minded main/renderer boundary** (from prior work in this repo) — IPC channel allowlists, integrity boot path, renderer network lockdown patterns in `main.js`—treat this as a **differentiator** and keep it regression-tested.

---

## Audit findings (themes, not nitpicks)

| Theme | Evidence / signal | Risk |
|--------|-------------------|------|
| **God-object UI shell** | `App.jsx` is very large (multi-thousand lines, huge `Suspense` surface) | Harder reviews, merge conflicts, slower onboarding, harder reasoning about panel state |
| **Design system is “locked” but fragile** | Arc test allows **≤1** arbitrary hex and **≤10** arbitrary px in `components/*.jsx` | One flashy PR can fail CI; good— but also signals **legacy debt** concentrated in few files |
| **Accessibility vs automation** | Many `data-testid` usages; **`aria-` / `role=`** appears on far fewer component files in a coarse count | Keyboard/screen-reader quality may lag visual polish |
| **Logging in UI** | `console.log` in e.g. `ConversationDNA.jsx`; many `console.warn` in error paths | Prod build strips them, but **dev noise** and inconsistent **user-visible** error reporting |
| **Bundle concentration** | Post-build `index-*.js` still **> 500 kB** after minify | First paint / parse cost on modest hardware; mobile-class devices if you ever ship web-adjacent |
| **Merge follow-up** | You merged `origin/master` while **keeping “ours”** on hot paths | PR #54–style deltas on overlapping files may need a **targeted port** so you do not silently miss trust/UI fixes |

---

## Plan to make everything “even better” (prioritized)

### Phase 0 — Baseline and honesty (short, high ROI)

1. **Run the full gate you ship against** — At least once: `npm run verify:all` or your stricter `verify:ship` subset on a clean tree, and capture failures as a single backlog queue.  
2. **Reconcile post-merge gaps** — Diff `origin/master` (or `6e965a6`) against current `main.js` / `preload.js` / any file you force-kept in the merge; open tickets for each **security- or compliance-relevant** hunk not present on your branch.

### Phase 1 — UX and trust (user-visible “gold”)

1. **Error UX contract** — Replace ad-hoc `console.warn` in storage/clipboard paths with a **small toast or inline error** pattern + centralized logger hook (dev-only detail).  
2. **Accessibility pass (incremental)** — Pick **10 highest-traffic components** (chat shell, command palette, settings drawer, modals with focus trap). For each: focus order, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, escape to close, visible focus rings using **existing** Tailwind tokens (no new hex drift).  
3. **Remove / gate debug logs** — Strip or `import.meta.env.DEV`-guard `console.log` in large panels (`ConversationDNA` and similar) so devtools stay readable.

### Phase 2 — Architecture (long-term velocity)

1. **Decompose `App.jsx`** — Introduce a **`ShellLayout`** (chrome + providers), **`PanelHost`** (open/close + Suspense boundaries), and **`usePanelRoutes`** (or similar) so `App.jsx` becomes orchestration, not 6k lines of JSX. 2. **Panel loading model** — Collapse deep `Suspense` nesting where possible: one boundary per **layer** (e.g. “overlay stack”, “left rail”, “main”) instead of per-panel fireworks.  
3. **State boundaries** — You already have `useConnectionStore` and mood store patterns; document **when to use Zustand vs props vs Shell context** in a short internal doc (or comments in `ShellContext`) so new panels do not reintroduce prop drilling.

### Phase 3 — Performance and shipping quality

1. **Chunk strategy beyond vendors** — Add `manualChunks` rules for **heavy optional domains** (e.g. ecosystem consoles, mission control) *after* measuring with `rollup-plugin-visualizer` or Vite’s analyze mode—avoid random splitting.  
2. **React render hygiene** — Continue the memo/store pattern where **profiling** shows benefit; avoid blanket memo on tiny leaf components (noise).  
3. **E2E “smoke orbit”** — Keep `react-core` + `ui-controls-sweep` as mandatory on every PR; rotate one **domain spec** per day in CI to control wall time.

### Phase 4 — IP, narrative, and enterprise readiness (non-code but “product gold”)

1. **Single product story** — Align naming (Operator vs Pro vs NeuralShell) across `README`, in-app copy, and `docs/` so sales/engineering/security reviewers see one brand line.  
2. **Threat model + trust center** — One short doc: what runs in renderer vs main, what leaves the machine, how keys are stored—pairs well with your OMEGA / integrity narrative.  
3. **License and third-party** — Keep `npm run attribution:gen` / SBOM steps wired in release docs so “IP gold” is **auditable**, not aspirational.
